_comment: P(ClearType tuning) of a Windows machine: the (gamma x1000, enhanced
contrast x100) pair DirectWrite draws text with, drawn per seed from its
own stream (derive_cleartype_tuning). A weighted pool like every other
pool in this package: cumulative, in order, never reordered and never
shortened in place.
This is where real machines differ on canvas. Retail Firefox 151 never
changes a pixel between drawing and reading, and a small canvas (every
fingerprinting canvas) is drawn the same on the GPU and in software:
measured 2026-10-24 on signed retail 151.0, gfx.canvas.accelerated true and
false gave the same text and the same shapes. What moves a canvas from one
Windows machine to the next, with the same fonts, is how the text edge is
drawn, and that is the user's ClearType tuning.
Every key is a row of coverage_ladders.json, measured on retail Firefox
151; profile.coverage_ladder refuses any other. The 12 renders are real
and different (12 text hashes, random-pixel readback 0/64 on each, geometry
unchanged, 2026-10-24).
ALL THE MASS IS ON 1800/100, THE UNTUNED MACHINE, DELIBERATELY. That is a
data statement, not a placeholder: there is no measured share of Windows
users who ran the ClearType Text Tuner, and inventing one is the guess
this codebase keeps having to undo (cpt_touch_given_class.json carries
the same note). The other measured keys are listed at 0 so that a
measured share is an edit to the numbers in this file: no Python change,
no browser rebuild, and every seed that keeps the untuned row keeps its
canvas.

source.untuned: retail 151.0 on a machine with HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Avalon.Graphics absent draws the 1800/100 ladder (coverage_ladders.json source; re-measured 2026-10-24)
